correctness.rationale: Orthogonal Gaussian invariance puts the 3x3 symmetric A in a Ritz diagonal 2+1 block and the sketched 2x2 M in diagonal + q(t1,t2) form. The discriminant D<0 is an indefinite homogeneous quadratic in three independent standard normals because F^-1g has bivariate Cauchy density (2pi)^-1(1+||q||^2)^-3/2. The K quadratic has three vanishing principal 2x2 minors, negative determinant for dt1t2 !=0 and two positive/one negative eigenvalues; u+v=1. Conditioning on normal Z3, the Gaussian measure of the ellipse is dominated by a disk of area pi Z3^2 sqrt(uv)<=pi Z3^2/2, giving 1-sqrt(2/3). Strict rearrangement and the product determinant imply equality precisely |t1|=|t2|=beta-alpha with alpha<beta. Degenerate d=0 or t1t2=0 gives zero risk. The displayed SPD example has positive Schur complement 14/3; the result is only for fixed U, ambient 3 and two Gaussian rows.
residual_risks: Finite experiments do not prove unrestricted statements; proof deductions above carry general assertion.
